basis: Defined as productive HPV infection of vulvar epithelium; reproductive location has no organ axis.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; axonal degeneration and ataxia in 3/4, cerebellar atrophy in 2/4. Hearing loss and muscle atrophy each only 1/4.
Umbrella of inherited fatty-acid oxidation and ketogenesis defects; direct hepatic, muscular and cardiac damage varies substantially among subtypes.
Powassan virus infection causing encephalitis defines both CNS involvement and infectious mechanism.
Defined by intellectual disability, developmental delay and frequent seizures; hypotonia does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Arthrochalasia EDS is defined by severe joint laxity, congenital dislocations and abnormal extensible, fragile skin.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis in 1/2 annotated patients supports skeletal involvement, although the frequency estimate is imprecise.
Inherited acanthosis nigricans directly affects skin; familial disease alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias; seizures are reported in only 1/5.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability defines neurologic involvement.
Choroid plexus neoplasm arises within the brain; increased mitotic activity defines the atypical subtype.
Patellar defects, neurodevelopmental impairment and renal malformations define the syndrome. Laryngomalacia affects 6/19 (~32%), supporting airway involvement.
Defined by congenital fibular absence, ectrodactyly and associated limb skeletal malformations.
Primary cutaneous melanoma; metastatic risk does not establish common direct damage to another organ axis.
Structural breaks in retinal Bruch membrane define an ocular disorder; the neurologic ancestor does not establish brain involvement.
Central failure to recognize auditory information despite usually normal hearing; no intrinsic ear disease is established.
Congenital shortening and fusion of digits in both hands and feet; ancestry specifies nonsyndromic brachydactyly.
Persistent central vestibular motion-perception dysfunction; peripheral ear injury is not established. Occasional visual and gastrointestinal symptoms do not support additional axes.
Complex I disorder; brain atrophy, hearing impairment and rod-cone dystrophy each in 1/1 annotated patient. Respiratory insufficiency alone does not establish intrinsic lung injury.
Retinal lymphoma defines an ocular lymphoid-cell malignancy; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Malignancy of hormone-producing Leydig cells, the endocrine component of the gonad; metastatic sites are not established as commonly damaged.
Supplied ancestry identifies a syndrome of corneal disease, muscular atrophy and nephropathy; neuropathy is not sufficiently established by the conflicting related synonym.
Peroxisomal disorder; neurologic dysfunction, hearing loss and retinal degeneration each commonly exceed 30%. Hepatic involvement also occurs commonly but is omitted under the four-axis cap.
Mature teratoma arises in the CNS; differentiated tissues within the tumour do not establish disease of their corresponding organs.
Genetic podocyte disease with nephrotic syndrome in 2/2 and kidney failure in 1/2. Extrarenal findings lack frequencies sufficient for inclusion; immune mediation is not established.
